history.summary: Sai Upvan ('the Sai grove') is a Sathya Sai temple on a wooded campus on Grand Trunk Road near the Hindon river, Ghaziabad. Sai activities in the city began in the early 1970s with bhajans, bal vikas and village seva projects; after Ghaziabad became a district in 1974 the Sri Sathya Sai Seva Organisations began work toward a dedicated Sai centre, and Bhagawan Sri Sathya Sai Baba visited the city in 1982 en route to Rishikesh. The temple is known for its large Sai statue and green, forest-like surroundings. NOTE: no published source gives the temple's exact construction year; coordinates are approximate (street-level geocode). Opening hours conflict between sources: most list 5:00 AM-9:30 PM (Tuesday till 10:30 PM), one lists 5:00 AM-10:30 PM daily (verify).

name: Sai Upvan Temple
town_description: Ghaziabad is a major industrial city in western Uttar Pradesh, just east of Delhi on the Grand Trunk Road and the banks of the Hindon river. Part of the National Capital Region and often called the 'Gateway of Uttar Pradesh', it grew around railway workshops and industry; its old-city and Mohan Nagar areas sit on the Delhi-Meerut corridor with Red Line metro and highway access.

travel.airport: Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi (~40 km)
travel.railway: Mohan Nagar (~1.35 km); Ghaziabad Junction (~8 km)
travel.road: On Grand Trunk Road (NH 9) on the Delhi-Meerut corridor; nearest metro: Hindon River (Red Line, ~0.2 km)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Sai Baba's birthday on 23 November is the major celebration
